transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okafor, thank you for coming in today. I also want to thank you for bringing your daughter along. I asked you both to come in because I have some important information to share regarding the developmental screening for your grandson.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Of course. We've been wondering why we haven't heard anything since that first call.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a difficult conversation to have, and I want to be very direct with you. We made a mistake in how we handled the referral process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What exactly do you mean by that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: After the first appointment was declined, the referral was marked as completed in our electronic system. Because of that, no further follow-up attempts were made. Essentially, the system showed the task as done when it actually wasn't.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. You are telling me that because we missed one date, the entire process just stopped? I'm a retired teacher, I know how bureaucracy works, but this seems like a significant lapse in care.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize. I am responsible for overseeing these referrals, and I failed to ensure the follow-up occurred. I am very sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand you're apologizing, but I'm more concerned about the time lost. My grandson is at a critical age for these interventions. Do you have any idea how long this has been sitting in the system as completed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It has been four months since the initial referral.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Four months. That is a quarter of a year. I feel incredibly frustrated that we trusted the clinic to manage this and it just vanished.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you actually understand? We were waiting for a phone call that was never going to come because someone clicked a box.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is frustrating. Now, to get this moving, I have already called the screening center.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You've called them? When can we actually get an appointment?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have a provisional slot for next Tuesday at ten in the morning. I need you to call my office by tomorrow afternoon to confirm if that time works for your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tuesday could work. But what happens if this happens again? How do I know that other things aren't being marked as finished when they aren't?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am reviewing all pending referrals in my current patient list to ensure no one else was missed. I will also be setting up a weekly manual audit of the screening logs so we aren't relying solely on the software.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That sounds like a start. But I want a written record of this error and the plan to fix it for my own files.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly provide that. I will draft a summary of the error and the corrective steps we've taken and send it to your portal by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. And the appointment? If we confirm tomorrow, is it guaranteed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. Once you call the office and confirm, I will personally call the specialist to lock in that ten o'clock slot.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the apology, but the loss of time is the real issue here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. Now, regarding the appointment on Tuesday, is there anything else you need from me to make that happen?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I think the priority is just getting the child seen. I will call tomorrow.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under pushback, though pacing is slightly brisk toward the end.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly and in lay language, but the resident never performs a comprehension check (e.g., 'Does that make sense?').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I apologize', 'I am very sorry'), takes personal responsibility, and maintains accountability despite the patient's frustration.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand', 'It is frustrating') but does not name specific emotions back to the patient or deeply engage emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides specific next steps (appointment Tuesday), timelines (call by tomorrow, portal by Friday), the patient's role (confirming the time), and a prevention plan (manual audits).
